# Review: PR #1361 — feat(auctions): auction order details — settlement status display & auction-aware order actions

Head SHA: `79010e92aed58dc42ee19c8162d953b9745f04c1`
Author: maxime-tt
Reviewer: worker-reviewer-kimi (Kimi, Moonshot AI family)
Base: `auctions`

## Verdict

**APPROVED**

CI is green: e2e-grep / footprint / prettier / security-scan / unit-integration all pass. Local `bun run test:unit` reproduces the reported 1386 pass / 0 fail across 94 files (including the new `e2e/scenarios/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts` production-validity gate). The two P1 blockers from the 2026-09-13 re-review are closed by code inspection and by targeted regression tests.

## What was checked

### P1a — `pending` settlement must not authorize fulfillment

Verified. The classifier at `src/lib/auction/settlementDescriptor.ts:583-596` requires the positive classification `latestSettlementValidity === 'valid'`, not merely a settled phase. Combined with `classifyPhase() === 'settled'` and `hasMatchedClaimOrder`, a retained-but-pending settlement (raw kind-1024 structurally OK but matching path release unvalidated/unobserved) fails closed. The `pending` regression is exercised both as a unit test (`src/lib/__tests__/settlementDescriptor.test.ts:1375`, RED at the previous head per the PR body, GREEN here) and against the production fixture events at `e2e/scenarios/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts:408-415` ("a settlement whose matching path release is not observed yet grants NO authority").

The `verifiedBadge` for the same input is `'verifying'`, which is what `AuctionSettlementStatus` surfaces as "Validating…" instead of a misleading positive status — confirmed by `orderSettlementStatusView.ts:37`.

### P1b — authority must be bound to the order being mutated

Verified. `getAuctionFulfillmentAuthority` returns an object with `claimOrderId`, and `OrderActions` now passes the full object as `auctionAuthority` (`OrderDetailComponent.tsx:580-583, 641`) and binds it via `claimOrderAuthorizesFulfillment(auctionAuthority, order.order.id)` (`OrderActions.tsx:93`). Collapsing to a boolean would have let authority from claim A unlock sibling order B on the same coordinate; this is the exact regression covered at `settlementDescriptor.test.ts:1424-1436` ("a sibling order on the same coordinate stays non-fulfillable when claim A is canonical") and at lines 1413-1422. `claimOrderAuthorizesFulfillment` also fails closed on `null`/`undefined`/missing order id/missing claim order id (`settlementDescriptor.ts:612-619`, tested at lines 1438-1448).

Confirms worth noting:

- **Suppression is order-local, not page-local.** Cancel/Confirm are gated by `showCancel = canCancel && !isAuction` and `showConfirm = canConfirm && !isAuction` (`OrderActions.tsx:117-118`). Auction orders therefore never render these buttons; product orders are untouched, and `canProcess`/`canShip`/`canReceive` are not modified for products (`OrderActions.tsx:94-100`).
- **`canShip` retains the binding.** `isSeller && status === PROCESSING && !hasBeenShipped && (!isAuction || auctionAuthorized)` keeps the same claim-order binding across both mutation steps (`OrderActions.tsx:100`).
- **Stock dialog gated by `!isAuction`** (`OrderActions.tsx:318`), which keeps auction orders from tripping product stock edits.

### Other observations

- The `toRawEvent()` fix is correct: `fetchAuctionClaimOrders()` returns `applesauceIo.fetchEvents()` results, which are plain event-likes, so the prior `.rawEvent()` call would have been a runtime TypeError. The new flow at `OrderDetailComponent.tsx:531` calls `toRawEvent(o)` on claim orders, and lines 469-509 do the same on bids/verdicts/settlements/path-releases before parsing. Consistent with `src/lib/nostr/eventLike` providing the bridge.
- The four review items @maximotodev raised at `9b35d72a` (settlement status from validated descriptor, suppress Cancel/Confirm for PENDING claim, broad detector stays presentation-only, fixture production-validity) are all closed in this head — the PR body maps each to its fix commit, and my spot checks of items 1, 2, and 4 against the code agree.
- The four @felixfelix-bot RISK/NIT items from 2026-08-14 are unchanged at this head (and acknowledged in the PR body as still open or not applicable). None blocks.

## Findings

No BLOCK/RISK findings. Three NITs, all non-blocking; flagging them inline so they can be picked up in follow-ups:

- [NIT] `src/queries/orders.tsx:236-244` — `isValidATag(coords)` after `getCoordsFromATag(coords)` succeeded is unreachable: `isValidATag` simply re-calls `getCoordsFromATag` under try/catch, so it cannot fail here. Either drop the second check or replace the first block with a single `getCoordsFromATag` inside a try/catch.
- [NIT] `src/components/orders/OrderDetailComponent.tsx:443-445` — three auction hooks (`useAuctionBids`, `useAuctionSettlements`, `useAuctionPathReleases`) are called unconditionally at top level on `OrderDetailComponent`, even for plain product orders. They are gated by `enabled:` in the underlying `queryOptions`, so no network traffic is generated on product orders, but the inconsistency is unforced. Hoisting them into a child component rendered only when `isAuctionOrder` is true (or gating via `auctionCoordinates + enabled:` consistently with `useAuctionVerdicts` below, which uses `isAuctionOrder`) would tighten the wire-up.
- [NIT] `src/components/orders/OrderDetailComponent.tsx:734` — Auction order card hardcodes `Quantity: 1`. The product branch uses `quantityMap`. For kind-30408 listings the quantity is structurally 1 today, but if multi-quantity auctions ship later this line will underreport. Acknowledged in the PR body as still open; not a blocker.

[INFO] The settlement card content itself is not asserted in the e2e suite (`e2e/tests/order-detail.spec.ts` has the relevant assertion commented out with `TODO: Needs CVM configuration for seeded bid to show up`). The specs therefore prove the routing, lifecycle, and authority behavior end-to-end, but not the phase text on the rendered card. This is pre-existing and acknowledged as a known coverage gap in the PR body.

## Gate 2.5

Cold-audit pass (in-run delegate, read-only file inspection against the head checkout): **AUDIT: PASS** — the three primary claims (P1a fail-closed on pending settlement, P1b order-id-bound authority object, presentation-only auction detection) verified independently against the code at this head. No BLOCK/RISK found in the diff.

Note: this run's Gate 2.5 was executed in-family (delegated subagent inherits the parent profile's model). The cleanest cross-family variant (glm-5.3) requires a kanban hand-off; per current operator guidance, in-run delegate is the prescribed Gate 2.5 mechanism for this profile.
modifying package.json: adding e2e/scenarios is NOT correct to add as part of the unit test suite...

# Review — PR #1361: feat(auctions): auction order details — settlement status display & auction-aware order actions (supersedes #1226)

- Repo: `PlebeianApp/market`
- Base: `auctions` @ `d0542215848cf7d69835a4f54703733b6924f001`
- Head: `cb1972f96caa80e8bf82d45e433fad888eabd8d3`
- Size: 13 files, +2215 / −61
- `mergeable_state`: `blocked`

## Verdict

No blocking **code** finding. The two P1s the 2026-09-13 re-review raised are genuinely closed at this head, and the `package.json` objection that produced the last `CHANGES_REQUESTED` is resolved by construction. What still stands between this head and merge is **process**, not implementation: a stale PR body/in-code reference that contradicts the code this PR now ships (§G merge condition), an unsigned architecture decision that needs a human ruling, and a stale blocking review anchored to an old SHA. I am submitting this as a bot `COMMENT` — it is a soft block and does not hold the merge.

## Review limits (what I did and did not do)

Verified by reading the diff at the pinned head and the prior thread (`conversation.json`):

- full `diff.patch` for all 13 files; hunk-by-hunk line accounting for `src/components/orders/OrderActions.tsx`, `src/components/orders/OrderDetailComponent.tsx`, `src/queries/orders.tsx`, `src/lib/auction/settlementDescriptor.ts`, `src/lib/auction/auctionOrderFixture.ts`, `e2e/scenarios/index.ts`;
- the three existing reviews (felixfelix-bot `COMMENTED`, Franchovy `APPROVED` then `CHANGES_REQUESTED`), all anchored to `79010e92`;
- that no `package.json` change is present at this head (grep of `diff.patch` and `files.txt`/`files.json`);
- call-site counts by grep (see below).

Not done, and not claimed:

- **No live/network/deployment check.** No CI conclusion, no preview, no relay probe.
- **No local reproduction and no test run.** The body's `1386 pass / 0 fail`, `13 passed (2.4 m)` and `tsc` baseline are **unverified** here. (Note the skill records `bunx tsc --noEmit` OOMing in this environment, so the body's `tsc` claim is not independently checkable from this session either.)
- **ADR text not readable in this environment.** `adr.list` confirms `ADR-0003-auctions-comprehensive-validation-protocol.md` and `ADR-0004-auction-settlement-descriptor.md` exist on the base branch, but no `auctions` checkout and no ADR contents are present in this working directory, so I could **not** read `ADR-0003`/`ADR-0004` decision or deferral text. Anything ADR-conformance-shaped below is labelled accordingly.

## 🧑⚖️ HUMAN SIGN-OFF REQUIRED

```
decision:      order surfaces now derive auction fulfillment authority from the validated
               settlement descriptor + canonical claim (new getAuctionFulfillmentAuthority),
               with "Process" reachable at PENDING and no generic CONFIRMED for auctions;
               new normative spec text AUCTIONS.md §4.3.3; new SettlementPhase
               'griefed-no-fallback'.
authorised by: NOT VERIFIED. ADR-0003 and ADR-0004 exist on the base branch (adr.list),
               but their text was not readable in this review environment, so I cannot say
               whether they already authorise — or defer — order-surface fulfillment
               authority. conversation.json contains no maintainer comment on this PR
               approving the decision.
```

This is an implementation PR that **adds normative spec content** (`AUCTIONS.md` §4.3.3, +82 lines, `diff.patch:5`) and a new authority concept, so it gets the visibility block regardless. The earlier maintainer feedback the body cites (`@maximotodev`, items "at `9b35d72a`") is review feedback on prior heads, not an architecture sign-off, and none of it appears in this PR's own review thread. The decision may well already be covered by ADR-0003/0004 — a maintainer ruling will settle it; I am not withholding the review over it.

## Required before merge

1. **Stale description and in-code reference contradict the shipped tree.** The body says the new regression gate is `e2e/scenarios/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts` and that "this file runs in `bun run test:unit`". At this head that file does **not** exist; the gate is `src/lib/__tests__/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts` (`files.json`, added +280), and `e2e/ARCHITECTURE.md` — added by this same PR — states the gate is `src/lib/__tests__/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts` and that it runs "with no change to `package.json`". The same wrong path is hard-coded in the PR's own new file: `src/lib/auction/auctionOrderFixture.ts:133` ("See `e2e/scenarios/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts` for that cross-validation"). **Requested:** update the body and `auctionOrderFixture.ts:133` to the shipped path. This is the same change Franchovy asked for; the body should describe the resolution, not the pre-resolution layout. (Per `docs/PR_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md §G:145` a stale PR description is a merge condition; the stale doc/comment half is housekeeping, not gated.)

2. **Maintainer ruling on the sign-off block above** — because the ADR text could not be compared here, this is the one thing a bot cannot close out.

## Non-blocking findings

- **Authority vs descriptor could diverge (question, unverified).** `getAuctionFulfillmentAuthority()` is synchronous and reuses `deriveState(input)` (`src/lib/auction/settlementDescriptor.ts:583`, `:590`, `:592`), while the settlement card calls the **async** `getSettlementDescriptor(descriptorInput)` (`OrderDetailComponent.tsx:557`), which fetches mint keysets. The PR's comment asserts "the mint-keyset fetch … only affects path-release proof decoding, which is not part of the fulfillment transition" (`settlementDescriptor.ts:583` block). I could not read `deriveState`/`validatePathRelease` at this base, so I cannot confirm that the synchronous `latestSettlementValidity === 'valid'` can never be **more** permissive than the async descriptor's classification — i.e. that a settlement the card would later show as invalid cannot already have unlocked `Process`. The `pending`/absent-path-release direction is clearly fail-closed (tested at `settlementDescriptor.test.ts` P1a case and `auctionOrderFixture.test.ts`). **Requested:** one sentence confirming the two paths share the validity classification, or a test that drives an async-invalid / sync-valid divergence.

- **`SettlementPhase` gained a new member; consumer sweep unverified.** `'griefed-no-fallback'` was added (`settlementDescriptor.ts:24`) and `classifyPhase` now returns it instead of collapsing into `'cancelled'` (`:530-531`). The only consumer updated in this PR is `orderSettlementStatusView.ts`. Because no workflow runs `tsc`, a consumer that switches on `SettlementPhase` without a default fails silently. **Requested:** confirm every consumer (auction detail surfaces etc.) handles the new member; this is a behavioural change to shared code, not just an order-page display change.

- **`settlementValidating` latches on descriptor error.** `descriptorFailed` is only cleared on a later success, but the effect re-runs only when `descriptorInput` changes (`OrderDetailComponent.tsx:551-571`, `:591`), so one transient `getSettlementDescriptor` throw pins the card at "Validating…" with no retry. Minor reliability, no authority impact.

## Carry-over NITs (still open at this head)

- Redundant validation in `src/queries/orders.tsx`: `getCoordsFromATag(coords)` already succeeded inside the `try`, then `if (!coords || !isValidATag(coords)) return null` re-runs the same parse (`orders.tsx:242`); the second check cannot fail where the first succeeded. Same shape at `OrderDetailComponent.tsx:444`.
- Three auction hooks called unconditionally at the top of `OrderDetailComponent` even for product orders: `useAuctionBids('', 500, auctionCoordinates || '')` and siblings (`OrderDetailComponent.tsx:446-448`). Gated by `enabled:` downstream per the prior review, so no wire traffic, but the inconsistency is unforced.
- Hardcoded `Quantity: 1` in the auction item card (`OrderDetailComponent.tsx:737`), vs `quantityMap` in the product branch.

## Fixture gate — worth tightening the wording

`assertAuctionOrderFixtureValid` calls `validatePathRelease` with `skipCashuTokenCheck: true` and hardcodes `winningBidNut7State: 'spent'` (`auctionOrderFixture.ts` gate block). That is defensible (the token decode is the seller's redemption-time check; the fixture never redeems), but `e2e/ARCHITECTURE.md` and the fixture doc present the gate as running "the production cross-event validators" without naming the skip. A real validator would decode the token. The fixture still cannot seed a chain that a real client could not have produced *for the parts that matter to this feature*, but the docs overstate the gate slightly. Non-blocking; ask the author to name the skip in `e2e/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## What this head gets right (credited)

- **P1a closed.** Authority requires the positive classification `latestSettlementValidity === 'valid'` (`settlementDescriptor.ts:590-592`), so a retained-but-`pending` settlement fails closed exactly like `invalid`. Covered by both a unit case (`settlementDescriptor.test.ts`, "PENDING … grants NO fulfillment authority") and the production fixture direction (`auctionOrderFixture.test.ts`, same fixture with `pathReleases: []`).
- **P1b closed at the right seam.** There is exactly **one** production call site of `getAuctionFulfillmentAuthority` (`OrderDetailComponent.tsx:584`) and exactly **one** production call site of `claimOrderAuthorizesFulfillment` (`OrderActions.tsx:95`), at the mutation boundary; the object is never collapsed to a boolean. `canProcess` (`:97`) and `canShip` (`:102`) both require the binding for auctions, and `Cancel`/`Confirm` are suppressed for auctions only (`:119-120`), with product orders unchanged.
- **The seeded auction order is published as the canonical claim order** (`e2e/scenarios/index.ts` auction branch, using `buildAuctionClaimOrderTags`), so the E2E exercises the authority path rather than the generic `isSeller && CONFIRMED` gate. I traced the seed ladder: auction orders still receive Processing/Shipped/Delivered status updates (those `if`s are not type-gated), while only the generic `CONFIRMED` update and the product payment-request/receipt block are product-only (`e2e/scenarios/index.ts:793` and the `else if (type === 'auction')` branch, `:297`). That is consistent with the new tests asserting a `confirmed`-staged auction order renders `Pending`.
- **Regression tests run in the unit suite without touching `package.json`** — `src/lib/__tests__/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts` and `src/queries/__tests__/orders.test.ts` are both under the `src` glob.

## Closed since the last review (dropped, per carry-over doctrine)

- **Franchovy's `CHANGES_REQUESTED` objection** ("modifying package.json: adding e2e/scenarios is NOT correct …", review `5291828374` @ `79010e92`) is addressed at this head: there is no `package.json` change anywhere in the diff, the gate test lives under `src/lib/__tests__/`, and `e2e/ARCHITECTURE.md` documents the deliberate no-`package.json` approach. The objection no longer applies to the code — but see the stale-body item above for the residual documentation mismatch.

## Merge-state note

`conversation.json` shows `CHANGES_REQUESTED` (Franchovy) and two other reviews all pinned to `79010e92`, with **no review at `cb1972f9`**. `mergeable_state: blocked` is consistent with that stale blocking review; the body notes the `quality` ruleset is disabled so GitHub does not auto-dismiss it. The code objection is resolved, but the blocking review remains anchored to the old SHA and needs a fresh review (or dismissal) before this head can land — a bot `COMMENT` does not clear it.

## Minimum before merge

- Fix the stale test path in the PR body and `src/lib/auction/auctionOrderFixture.ts:133`.
- Obtain a maintainer ruling on the sign-off block (whether ADR-0003/0004 already authorise order-surface fulfillment authority and the new `griefed-no-fallback` phase).
- Answer the sync-vs-async authority-classification question, or add a divergence test.
- Confirm no `SettlementPhase` consumer misses the new member.

## BLOCK (1) — `griefed_no_fallback` is still seller-derived, not validator-quorum-derived

**Status: STILL HOLDS at `d1a4a647`.**

`src/lib/auction/settlementDescriptor.ts:540-556`:

```
function classifyPhase(d: DerivedState): SettlementPhase {
  if (!d.ended) return 'bidding-open'
  if (d.hasLatestSettlement) {
    switch (d.settlementStatus) {
      case 'settled':              return 'settled'
      case 'reserve_not_met':      return 'reserve-not-met'
      case 'griefed_no_fallback':  return 'griefed-no-fallback'
      case 'cancelled':            return 'cancelled'
```

`d.settlementStatus` is `latestSettlement?.status` (`:468`), i.e. read straight from the seller-authored **kind-1024** settlement event. `isSettlementStructurallyValid` returns `'valid'` for that status on seller + root + coordinate alone (`:188`, "reserve_not_met and griefed_no_fallback: basic structural checks pass").

There is **no** derivation of grief from kind-30440 validator claims anywhere in this tree:
- `git grep griefed d1a4a647 -- src/` surfaces only the kind-1024 status enum (`schemas/auction/settlementEvents.ts:109`, `constants.ts:145`), the display map (`orderSettlementStatusView.ts:47`), and the seller-status switch above. No quorum path.
- `src/lib/auction/verdictQuorum.ts:56-57` classifies verdicts into confirm/condemn only — it has no `griefed`/`griefed_pending_fallback` claim kind, so grief cannot be quorum-derived today even if the descriptor asked it to.

Accepted **ADR-0004** at this head is explicit that this is wrong:
- §3 (`:19`): "`griefed_no_fallback` moves from seller-derived to validator-quorum-derived."
- §"Confidence" (`:298-302`): "The seller may still publish kind-1024 with `griefed_no_fallback` as a formality, but **the source of truth is the validator quorum**."
- §"Wave budget" (`:369-373`): "`griefed_no_fallback` is determined by validator quorum (kind-30440 `griefed` claims), not by the seller's kind-1024 … the seller's kind-1024 with `griefed_no_fallback` is a confirmation, not the source of truth."

**Why it matters:** a single seller event moves the order card to the distinct, accusatory **"Griefed (No Fallback)"** label (`orderSettlementStatusView.ts:47`), publicly branding a buyer as having griefed, with no independent quorum. The seller is a counterparty to the outcome being labelled.

**Required fix (either is acceptable):**
1. Derive grief in `deriveState` from kind-30440 `griefed` / `griefed_pending_fallback` claims at or above `auction.auditorQuorum`, and drive `classifyPhase`'s grief branch from that consensus (requires extending `verdictQuorum.ts` to expose the grief claim family); **or**
2. Keep seller-declared grief collapsed to a non-accusatory state until quorum derivation exists — do not render the distinct accusatory label from a seller event alone.

Either way, add a test proving a lone seller `griefed_no_fallback` does **not** produce the "Griefed (No Fallback)" display state. Note `src/lib/__tests__/settlementDescriptor.test.ts:683` ("closed (griefed_no_fallback)") currently locks in the *unfixed* behavior and must be updated with the fix.

This was **BLOCK 2** of the #1226 consolidated verdict. It was raised there as a cross-track disagreement (the correctness track had marked the griefed phase "reviewed, no issue" because it verified the phase stays distinct from `cancelled` — which it does, and which ADR-0004 also requires). The two readings differ on *what was tested*: display separation vs. the source of the state. ADR-0004 §3/§369-373 settles it — the source must be quorum.

### B2 — "Griefed (No Fallback)" is still seller-decided, not quorum-decided **[BLOCK]**

This still holds, and the prior note understated its cost. Confirmed mechanism, both ends:

1. **The status is read straight off the seller-authored kind-1024.**
   `settlementDescriptor.ts:453-468` reduces `settlements` and takes
   `settlementStatus = latestSettlement?.status`. `settlements` are
   `ParsedSettlementEvent` (kind 1024, `constants.ts:41`), and `status` is a
   five-line zod enum field (`schemas/auction/settlementEvents.ts:109`). No kind-30440
   input reaches this decision — `input.verdicts` is consumed only by
   `computeValidatedBids`.

2. **No grief quorum can form even in principle.** `griefed` and
   `griefed_pending_fallback` *are* in `VALIDATOR_CLAIMS` (`constants.ts:163-164`), but
   they are in neither `VALIDATOR_CONFIRM_CLAIMS` (`:177`) nor
   `VALIDATOR_CONDEMN_CLAIMS` (`:180`), and `computeVerdictQuorum`
   (`verdictQuorum.ts:56-57`) only tallies those two sets. A validators' grief claim
   therefore produces a *neutral* verdict — it can never become a quorum signal, and
   nothing maps a quorum back to `griefed_no_fallback`.

This contradicts **ADR-0004** directly:

> `griefed_no_fallback` | Validator quorum (kind-30440) | Network consensus | Requires proving no path release was observed anywhere — needs quorum
> — ADR-0004:298

> **`griefed_no_fallback` moves from seller-derived to validator-quorum-derived.** […] The descriptor determines grief from `griefed` quorum in kind-30440 verdicts, not from the seller's kind-1024 claim.
> — ADR-0004:301-305 (restated at :369-373)

**Why this is a blocker, not a nit.** `isSettlementStructurallyValid` returns
`'valid'` for `griefed_no_fallback` on structural checks alone
(`settlementDescriptor.ts:186-189` — seller, root, coordinate only, no path-release or
bid-chain evidence), and grief is deliberately exempt from the B3
reserve-meeting-bid guard (`:181-186`). So a **seller-signed kind-1024 with
`status=griefed_no_fallback` classifies as validated unconditionally** and
`classifyPhase` returns `'griefed-no-fallback'` (`:552-553`). A seller can close an
auction that a bidder validly won and the order page will present "Griefed (No
Fallback)" as a validated terminal outcome to both the buyer and any fallback bidder.
That is the exact seller-spoofable negative ADR-0004 exists to prevent.

The test currently **encodes** the violation rather than catching it:
`__tests__/settlementDescriptor.test.ts:683-691` seeds grief purely via
`makeSettlement({ status: 'griefed_no_fallback' })` with `verdicts: []` (the
`makeInput` default, `:281`) and asserts the grief outcome. A correct test needs a
kind-30440 grief quorum for the positive case and must assert that the seller-authored
claim alone does **not** reach this phase.
